chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Sahl, from his father, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man traveling to his estate, at a distance of two or three barīds, while his route passes by the estates of his paternal cousins: should he shorten the salat (prayer) and break the fast, or should he complete it and fast? He said: He should not shorten, nor should he break the fast.

key_terms.بَرِيدَيْنِ: two barīds, a unit of travel distance
key_terms.يُتِمُّ: he performs the salat (prayer) in full

ai.seo_question: When traveling to one’s estate and passing by relatives’ properties, should one shorten salat (prayer) and break the fast?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a person traveling to his estate while passing by the estates of his paternal relatives. The Imam عليه السلام rules that in this case he does not shorten the salat (prayer) and does not break the fast, indicating the legal effect of such travel circumstances on salat (prayer) and sawm (fasting).
